id: D14-0 gate: trees for the termination and low-current frames
author: first_agent (group manager)
entrant: 2026-10-05: 'treba detailnú analýzu všetkých shotov, celú postupnosť, odpoveď sa nachádza niekde tam'; 'urobiť parametrické grafy na časovej osi shotov, a nájsť korelácie'
finding_that_motivates: D13 anatomy of the S16 out-of-fold head errors on all 1.32M training frames (d13_shot_anatomy): the squared error is concentrated at the end of the record and at low current. li: 30 % in the last 3 frames, 63 % in the last 25 (0.5 s), 60 % at Ip < 0.6 peak (7.6 % of frames); q95: 38 % in the last 25, 57 % at Ip < 0.6 peak, 10 % in the first 3 frames; betaN: 33 % in the last 25; z_axis 36 %, volume 30 %. The tail regime (fewer than 25 frames to the record end, or Ip < 0.6 peak, or < 0.3 s since start) is 10.9 % of the frames and holds 64 % (li), 62 % (q95), 33 % (betaN) of the head error. Inside it the general D9 trees are nearly as good as the networks for li (SSE ratio 1.10, in-regime weight .41).
question: Do trees fitted only on the tail regime, with the frame's position in the record as two extra inputs, improve the blend there beyond the general D9 trees?
tail_regime: from_end < 25 or feature 62 (Ip / discharge peak) < 0.6 or feature 64 (seconds since discharge start) < 0.3; defined from inputs only, identical at test time.
extra_inputs: frames to the end of the record and frame index in the record (both follow from the test shot's own frame times).
trees: D9 setting A unchanged; fits and early stopping on tail frames only; targets li_scored, q95, beta_n, r_axis, z_axis, kappa, volume.

evaluation.variants: general = D9 trees A with one nested weight (the D9-0 result); regime = D9 trees A with separate nested weights in and outside the tail; special = tail trees in the tail (nested weight) and D9 trees A outside (own nested weight). Same head-level proxy and shot bootstrap (2000, seed 990) as D9-0.

rule: PASS if dS_proxy(special) - dS_proxy(general) >= +1e-5 with bootstrap P >= .95. PASS -> a deployment protocol adds the tail trees (and the regime weights) to the D9 blend, like for like on the 195-net. If only 'regime' beats 'general' by that margin, the regime weights alone are adopted for the next D9 build (no new fit needed). FAIL on both -> closed.
exposure: D13 anatomy and the in-regime weight of the general trees are known (computed from existing out-of-fold arrays). No tail-only fit exists at freeze.
